purpose: Separate the reusable continuity mechanisms in planning-with-files from its full multi-host Skill, Hook, transcript, persistence, completion-gate, and host-adapter system so that catalog count or one-click Skill installation cannot bypass dependency, privacy, authority, and lifecycle review.

payloadSurface.interpretation: The eighteen Skill paths are host and language projections of one system, not eighteen independent capability units. Every Skill body has a distinct hash, so the manager must select an exact projection and cannot infer parity from the shared declared name.

mechanismSlices.surface: task_plan.md, findings.md, progress.md plus optional isolated .planning/<id>/ state
mechanismSlices.reason: This is a concrete process-loss and fresh-session recovery mechanism that is not equivalent to a transient model plan.

mechanismSlices.surface: turn, tool, compact, permission, and stop lifecycle adapters
mechanismSlices.reason: The mechanism can reduce drift but also adds instruction recitation, token cost, Hook ordering, trust, and duplicate-injection risk.

mechanismSlices.surface: read-only parsing of Codex rollout JSONL, Claude project JSONL, or OpenCode SQLite by host projection
mechanismSlices.reason: It may place prior user, assistant, and tool excerpts back into model context and therefore crosses a broader local-data boundary than reading repository planning files alone.

mechanismSlices.surface: PLAN_ID, PWF_PLAN_ROOT, per-session sentinels, path containment, SHA-256 attestation, and ambiguity fail-closed behavior
mechanismSlices.reason: These controls directly address wrong-plan injection and tamper amplification without proving cross-host behavior parity.

mechanismSlices.surface: .mode, .stop_blocks, ledger-<agent>.jsonl, host-specific block or follow-up behavior
mechanismSlices.reason: Completion control changes stop authority and the exact source documentation describes AcceptanceCheck execution that was not found in the reviewed runtime source.

mechanismSlices.surface: twelve host projections, six language variants, separate Hook adapters, and divergent bodies
mechanismSlices.reason: Host-specific packaging is useful evidence, but shared naming and separate bodies do not establish one dependency-complete cross-host unit.

currentCodexObservation.meaning: The host exposes a Hook capability and separate trust boundary. This does not prove that the candidate adapter is configured, trusted, loaded, or protocol-compatible in Codex Desktop or any other host.

documentationImplementationFinding.claim: MIGRATION.md states that an attested allowlisted AcceptanceCheck command may be run by the completion gate.
documentationImplementationFinding.staticObservation: No AcceptanceCheck parser or executor was found in the reviewed runtime shell, PowerShell, Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript source at the pinned revision; only documentation and templates mention the field.

currentCapabilityOverlap.meaning: The candidate supplies stronger automatic file and Hook mechanisms than a plain planning Skill, but overlap does not prove equivalence, redundancy, superiority, retirement authority, or a residual self-authored gap.

managerBoundary.reason: A Skill-only manager projection would omit the separately shipped Codex Hook manifest and adapter directory, host Hook enablement and trust state, and Windows Python or Git Bash dependencies. Selecting among eighteen divergent SKILL.md paths is also an unresolved manager-path decision.
managerBoundary.nextSafeAction: Use the exact source as a split mechanism comparator. First build a zero-execution host and data-boundary protocol; only a later separately authorized isolated run may execute one exact host projection. Do not register or install the full source merely to increase portfolio count.
